summary: Query the messages FTS index in local search; it held matches no code path could reach.
reason: store.SearchMessages existed at internal/store/store.go and was correct, but had zero callers anywhere in the tree. search.go's empty-type branch queried only SearchUsergroups and SearchFiles despite a comment claiming it searched all FTS-enabled tables, and `--type messages` fell through to the generic db.Search. Meanwhile sync populates both messages and messages_fts. The result was a silent wrong answer: a term with rows in messages_fts returned "No results" with exit 0, indistinguishable from a genuine miss. Reproduced against a real synced database where messages_fts held 40 rows matching a term the CLI reported as absent. Two lines of wiring: a case for `--type messages`, and a messages block in the all-types branch. Messages are queried first in the all-types branch deliberately, because outputSearchResults truncates the aggregate to --limit and whatever runs first survives that cut — a bare `search <query>` is nearly always after messages, so letting usergroups and files crowd them out would reproduce the same practical failure with a different cause. This depends on slack-search-messages-matches: locally synced messages carry text and ts but no top-level title/name/identifier/id, so without that patch's isNilOrEmpty extension the newly-returned rows would be discarded by the emptiness filter and local search would still report nothing. Kept on the existing typed-table architecture rather than migrating to the generic resources table, which the current generator favours — a deliberate choice, since all eight of this CLI's novel analytics commands (digest, health, quiet, trends, funny, activity, response_times, threads_stale) read the typed store, and converting would break them for no user-visible gain. Wiring the index in also exposed that SearchMessages passed its query straight to FTS5, while Search, SearchUsergroups and SearchFiles all route through sanitizeFTSQuery. Harmless while the function had no callers; reachable once it had one. An unmatched double quote produced "SQL logic error: unterminated string" and NOT/OR/NEAR were honoured as real operators, so identical input meant different things depending on which index answered. It now sanitizes like its siblings, and an empty query short-circuits to no results rather than reaching FTS5.
validated_outcome: Verified against a real synced database: messages_fts held 40 rows matching 'task' and the CLI previously reported "No results"; it now returns exactly 40 for both the all-types branch and --type messages, matching the SQLite ground-truth count. A term absent from the index (0 rows in SQLite) still reports no results, so the fix does not over-report. --limit 5 and --limit 10 return 5 and 10 respectively, confirming aggregate truncation still applies. A hit and a genuine miss both exit 0, a miss being a legitimate empty result rather than an error. search_local_amend_test.go adds four cases driving the real search command against a throwaway store seeded via store.UpsertMessage — the command wiring rather than the store helper, which matters because the store was always correct and a store-level test would have passed against the broken build. The suite was confirmed to catch the regression: with the pre-fix search.go restored, two of the four cases fail with the exact "No results (source: local)" symptom. go build, go vet, gofmt and the full internal/cli suite all clean. FTS5 handling verified before and after: pre-fix, `unmatched " quote` errored with SQL logic error and `task NOT review` applied a real NOT operator; post-fix both are treated as literal text and return no results, while an ordinary term still returns the full 40 matches. Six syntax cases plus an ordinary-term control were added to search_local_amend_test.go, and the suite was confirmed to catch the regression — reverting store.go fails on the unmatched-quote case with the exact production error.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Typed-table search wiring in the generated search template
deferred_to_upstream.reason: cli-printing-press#1390 covers this defect family — the generated empty-type branch queries a subset of the available typed FTS sources while its comment claims otherwise. It was closed 2026-05-15, but a probe of press 4.29.0 output showed the mismatch still present and inverted: the regenerated branch calls only the generic db.Search while claiming to search typed tables too. Refiled with that evidence as cli-printing-press#3810 rather than treating this CLI as the outlier; #1390 remains the closed original.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: A resolved store architecture, generic or typed
deferred_to_upstream.reason: This CLI is half-converted: sync writes users and conversations into the generic resources table while messages go to a typed table, and the generated store drops typed tables entirely along with the messages sync that fills them. Until the generator settles on one model, any local-search fix is pinned to whichever half it happens to target. Flagged as an architecture decision rather than a bug, and deliberately not resolved here.

notes: Local search now covers messages, usergroups and files. Users and conversations remain unsearchable locally for a different reason: sync writes them into the generic resources table rather than their typed tables, so there is no per-type index for them to query. Separate defect, not addressed here.
